Profile by Refitting on a Grid

Source: R/profile.R
profile_grid.Rd

Selects the exact method of statmod_profile(): at every value of the grid the model is fitted again with the coefficients held at that value, with the tolerances, the inner optimizer and the outer criterion of the fit.

Usage

ProfileGrid(name = character(0), start = character(0))

profile_grid(start = c("neighbor", "fit", "both"))

Arguments

name

The short name of the method, a single string. The class constructor ProfileGrid() takes it, and profile_grid() sets it to "grid".

start

One of "neighbor" (the default), "fit" and "both".

Value

A ProfileGrid object, inheriting from profile_method, with the properties name ("grid") and start.

Details

The three starts differ in the coefficients from which each refit begins. "neighbor" starts the refit at a value from the refit of the adjacent value that lies nearer to the estimate, going outward from the estimate in both directions, so that the coefficients move little between two refits. The first value on each side starts from the coefficients of the fit. With several held coefficients the chains run along the first one, one pair of chains (below and above the estimate) for each combination of the values of the others. "fit" starts every refit at the coefficients of the fit, with the held ones set to the value of the point; the points are then independent of each other. "both" runs the two and keeps, at every point, the refit with the larger penalized log-likelihood, at twice the cost. A profile with several local maxima, as that of a break-point has, can be reached from one start and missed from the other.

With cores greater than one in statmod_profile(), the chains of "neighbor" and the points of "fit" are distributed over worker processes.

See also

statmod_profile(), profile_method.

Examples

profile_grid()
#> <statmodels7::ProfileGrid>
#>  @ name : chr "grid"
#>  @ start: chr "neighbor"
profile_grid(start = "both")
#> <statmodels7::ProfileGrid>
#>  @ name : chr "grid"
#>  @ start: chr "both"
